pooled_hartung_knapp.why_it_is_shown: Handbook 6.5 section 10.10.4.5 recommends Hartung-Knapp where k is small. Shown ALONGSIDE the unadjusted interval, not instead of it. A FLOOR OF 1 is applied to the variance-inflation factor so the adjustment can never NARROW the interval below the unadjusted one.

heterogeneity.DIRECTION_TEST: NOT APPLICABLE -- I-squared is 0.0%, below the threshold at which the direction test is informative. The trials are consistent with a common effect and no heterogeneity caution is warranted. Applying one here would manufacture doubt the data do not support, which is the mirror failure of ignoring heterogeneity that matters.
heterogeneity.how_to_read_this_at_low_k: At k=2 or k=3 these statistics are weak evidence about consistency in EITHER direction. A low value means the estimates are CONSISTENT WITH a common effect, not that one is demonstrated.
heterogeneity.tau2_estimator: REML -- copied from this block's declared `estimator`, which is the authoritative record of how the pool was computed. NOT inferred: an object that declared no estimator would be left undeclared here, because the absence is itself the finding.
heterogeneity.i2_definition: UNDECIDABLE from this object. I-squared is 0 and Q is below the degrees of freedom, where the Higgins form is negative-and-clamped and the REML/metafor form is exactly zero -- BOTH DEFINITIONS GIVE 0 and nothing here distinguishes them. Recorded as undecidable rather than guessed.

primary.WHAT_THIS_POOL_IS_AND_IS_NOT: THIS IS NOT A POOL OF THE FIVE TRIALS THIS PAGE SEEDS. It is the DAPIVIRINE VAGINAL RING pair, which is the only subset sharing an intervention and a comparator. The page seeds five trials testing FOUR DIFFERENT THINGS: oral Truvada against placebo (NCT00625404, 33/1024 vs 35/1032), tenofovir 1% VAGINAL GEL against placebo gel (NCT00705679, 61/996 vs 70/996), the dapivirine ring against a placebo ring (the two pooled here), and NCT01386294 which posts NO RESULTS. Oral tablet, microbicide gel and vaginal ring are different interventions with different delivery, adherence and mechanism. POOLING ALL FIVE WOULD BE A CLASS CLAIM THE PAGE'S DATA CANNOT SUPPORT.
primary.the_person_years_primary_CHECKED: NCT00705679's registered primary 'Person-years of Follow-up' is NOT an effect measure, and that was flagged before reading. IT IS ONE OF TWO PRIMARIES: the same trial also registers 'Number of HIV-1 Infections' and posts 61/996 against 70/996. So the concern was real but not disqualifying -- the trial does register a usable endpoint. IT IS STILL NOT IN THIS POOL, because its INTERVENTION is a vaginal gel and not the ring.

published_synthesis_comparison.what_is_owed: No published synthesis of the two dapivirine ring trials has been read.

primary.what_this_does_not_establish: NOT that dapivirine ring PrEP works or does not work in this population -- NO RISK-OF-BIAS ASSESSMENT IS RECORDED and adherence, which dominates ring effectiveness, is not an outcome here. NOT anything about oral or gel PrEP, which are excluded above. NOT that the three excluded trials are poor: they answer different questions. NOT reliability at k=2 -- see Hartung-Knapp.

house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.estimator: REML with Hartung-Knapp, t on k-1 = 1 degree(s) of freedom (t = 12.7062)
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.THE_POINT_ESTIMATE_IS_UNCHANGED: The published point is 0.7030 and the house-rule point is 0.7030. THE NUMBER A READER REMEMBERS DOES NOT MOVE; what differs is the precision claim. That is why nothing downstream catches this -- every memorable quantity survives.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.variance_inflation_floor: A FLOOR OF 1 IS APPLIED TO THE VARIANCE-INFLATION FACTOR so the adjustment can never NARROW an interval below the unadjusted one. That guard is the recognised modification for exactly this instability, and its existence is evidence the small-k behaviour is a KNOWN problem with KNOWN handling rather than a novel judgement.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.no_rule_is_decided_here: The house rule is REML with Hartung-Knapp below k=10, settled days ago. Whether it means ALWAYS or WITH A FLOOR AT k=3 is a decision about this corpus, not a computation, and it has been referred rather than taken. BOTH INTERVALS STAND ON THIS PAGE UNTIL IT IS MADE. Nothing is unpublished and no reader is left with only the narrower one.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.what_this_means_for_this_pool: THE PUBLISHED INTERVAL EXCLUDES 1 AND THE HOUSE-RULE INTERVAL CROSSES IT. A SIGNIFICANCE VERDICT TURNS ON THE INTERVAL METHOD ALONE. A reader shown only the published interval has been told something firmer than the evidence supports; a reader shown only the wider one loses that the contributing trials agree. BOTH ARE HERE.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.read_the_width_with_care: AT k=2 HARTUNG-KNAPP USES t ON ONE DEGREE OF FREEDOM -- 12.7062 against the normal 1.9600 -- and the interval is enormously wider. That width is a property of the method at very few studies, not a measurement of this evidence. It is recorded so a reader can see it; it is NOT presented as the better interval.

POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.a_neither_trial_enrolled_an_adolescent: READ THIS BESIDE THE ESTIMATE. This review is named for ADOLESCENT GIRLS AND YOUNG WOMEN. BOTH CONTRIBUTING TRIALS SET A MINIMUM AGE OF 18 YEARS on their registrations -- NCT01539226 and NCT01617096, both FEMALE, both 18 to 45 years. NO PARTICIPANT UNDER 18 WAS ELIGIBLE FOR EITHER TRIAL. The estimate does not speak to adolescent girls, and GRADE indirectness is rated down for it.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.b_the_countries_are_right_even_though_th: Stated so the caution is not read wider than it is. The Ring Study ran in South Africa and Uganda; ASPIRE ran in Malawi, South Africa, Uganda and Zimbabwe. BY REGION THIS IS DIRECTLY THE POPULATION OF INTEREST. The indirectness is about AGE ALONE.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.c_the_effect_does_not_survive_the_small_: The unadjusted interval is RR 0.7030 (0.5660 to 0.8731) and EXCLUDES no difference. This project's Hartung-Knapp interval at k = 2 is 0.1725 to 2.8655 -- and NOT 0.4054 to 1.2191, which is metafor's RAW unfloored knha interval and was misattributed to this project in the first version of this note and INCLUDES it. THE HONEST READING OF THAT IS NARROW: at k = 2 the t critical value is 12.7062 and almost nothing survives the adjustment, so this is much weaker evidence against the result than the same disagreement would be at larger k. It is disclosed because a reader is entitled to both intervals, not because it overturns the estimate.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.d_no_external_check_exists_for_this_esti: A screen of eight records found NO published synthesis pooling HIV seroconversion across these two trials -- the five flagged syntheses are about adherence, acceptability and pregnancy outcomes. THIS ESTIMATE IS UNREPLICATED so far as this project has looked.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.e_a_registered_safety_co_primary_is_not_: Both registrations register adverse events as a SECOND PRIMARY OUTCOME. This review carries only the efficacy primary. That is a scope fact, not a defect in the estimate, and it is recorded so a reader does not read this page as a benefit-and-harm summary.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.b_the_countries_are_right_even_though_th: Corrected 2026-08-30 from ClinicalTrials.gov, read the same day: NCT01539226 is orgStudyId IPM 027, The Ring Study, n=1,959, and its registered locations are South Africa and Uganda; NCT01617096 is acronym ASPIRE, MTN-020, n=2,629, locations Malawi, South Africa, Uganda and Zimbabwe. The previous wording attached each trial's facts to the OTHER trial. ⛔ THESE TWO FIELDS ARE PROSE WITH NO NCT IN THE STRING, so neither this repo's NCT-keyed sweep nor the staging lane's gate could reach them -- both walk identifier keys. A name in free text has no key to walk. Found by rapidmeta-staging-33.

indirectness.reason: Downgraded one level for indirectness of POPULATION. The question is "in women", UNQUALIFIED. The evidence is women aged 18-45 (ClinicalTrials.gov, read 2026-08-30: both trials FEMALE, min 18 / max 45) recruited in four sub-Saharan African countries. A pooled effect from one region and one age band is not a direct answer to a question about women without qualification.
indirectness.what_decides_it_is_evidence_of_EFFECT_MO: This is not an extrapolation worry asserted from outside. ASPIRE reports, in its own words: "the efficacy of HIV-1 protection differed significantly according to age, with an efficacy of 61% (95% CI, 32 to 77; P<0.001) among women 25 years of age or older and 10% (95% CI, -41 to 43; P = 0.64) among those under the age of 25 years (P = 0.02 for interaction)." A SIGNIFICANT TREATMENT-BY-AGE INTERACTION WITHIN THE STUDIED RANGE. The Ring Study runs the same direction (hazard ratio 0.63 above 21 vs 0.85 at 21 or younger; P=0.43 for interaction) and proposes a mechanism that is not purely behavioural: "physiologic differences in the genital tract of younger women, lower adherence to ring use". WHEN A TRIAL DEMONSTRATES THAT ITS OWN EFFECT IS MODIFIED BY A POPULATION CHARACTERISTIC, TRANSFER TO UNSTUDIED VALUES OF THAT CHARACTERISTIC IS NOT SUPPORTED -- and age is not the only characteristic on which the studied population is narrow.
indirectness.what_would_have_to_differ_for_this_domai: Stated so the domain is falsifiable in both directions, because a domain that cannot be downgraded by any realistic evidence is not being assessed, and neither is one that cannot be cleared. EITHER (a) the review scopes its question to the population actually studied -- women aged 18-45 in high-incidence sub-Saharan African settings -- and says so in its title and question, not only in a rating note; OR (b) the treatment-by-age interaction is absent or shown to be an artefact of differential adherence that would not recur elsewhere. Neither holds today. (a) is an EDITORIAL act that changes what the review claims, and it must not be performed to move a letter.
indirectness.this_REVERSES_a_judgement_made_earlier_t: Hours earlier this domain was recorded NO_DOWNGRADE, on the reasoning that the trials ran "in the settings carrying the burden the intervention is for". That clause was challenged on review and does not survive: IT IS A REASON THE EVIDENCE IS APPROPRIATE, NOT A REASON IT IS DIRECT. The two are different claims and only the second is what this domain asks. The earlier judgement raised our own certainty from VERY LOW to LOW; testing it lowered it back. A favourable judgement that survives only until it is examined was never a judgement.

previous_judgement_2026_08_30.reason: Judged against the governing question -- "in women" -- which is the question the executed search was run on. Both contributing trials enrolled women (ClinicalTrials.gov, read 2026-08-30: NCT01539226 and NCT01617096, both FEMALE, 18-45 years), in the sub-Saharan African settings that carry the burden the intervention is intended for, comparing the dapivirine ring against a PLACEBO RING and reporting HIV-1 seroconversion -- the exact comparator and the exact outcome the question names. Population, intervention, comparator and outcome all match. No downgrade.
previous_judgement_2026_08_30.the_alternative_reading_and_what_it_woul: IF the question were AGYW -- adolescent girls and young women, as the topic identifier still says -- this domain would DOWNGRADE ONE LEVEL and the certainty would be VERY LOW rather than LOW. Both trials set a minimum age of 18, so NO GIRL UNDER 18 CONTRIBUTED A SINGLE PARTICIPANT-YEAR, and ASPIRE reported that protection was not demonstrated in its youngest enrolled stratum -- so the age gradient runs against assuming the result transfers downward. That is a real and material gap; it is simply a gap in a DIFFERENT question from the one this review asks.
previous_judgement_2026_08_30.declared_because_this_change_improves_ou: This judgement moves the certainty UP, from VERY LOW to LOW, and it replaces a DOWNGRADE recorded here earlier the same day. That direction is exactly why the reason is the executed search and not a preference: the rule -- the tested PICO governs -- was fixed BEFORE the rating was recomputed, and both readings are published side by side above so a reader can apply the other one and get VERY LOW without asking us.
previous_judgement_2026_08_30.judged_by: Explicit stored judgement. grade_engine refuses this domain by design and will not infer it.

indirectness.judged_by: Explicit stored judgement. grade_engine refuses this domain by design and will not infer it.
indirectness.reviewer_challenge_2026_08_30: A cross-family reviewer (openai) called this "partly sound, but DECISIVE is overstated", and the qualification is accepted. Two points stand against the strong form: ASPIRE’s interaction is significant (P = 0.02) while the Ring Study’s is only same-direction and NOT significant (P = 0.43), so the evidence for modification is one trial rather than two; and this is correctly NOT an inconsistency issue, because the two whole-trial estimates agree (I-squared 0%) -- it is a within-study subgroup difference, which is the more reliable kind, but it is still one study’s subgroup finding.
indirectness.the_better_move_that_is_now_owed: ⭐ The reviewer names an action stronger than the downgrade: where an effect modifier is credible and decision-relevant, Cochrane asks for SUBGROUP-SPECIFIC ESTIMATES AND SEPARATE SUMMARY-OF-FINDINGS ROWS, not a blunt downgrade of the pooled average. A reader aged 30 and a reader aged 19 are owed different numbers, and this review currently gives them one. The downgrade stands as the honest rating of the POOLED estimate; the age-stratified presentation is recorded as OWED.

load_bearing_quote_VERIFIED.document: Baeten JM et al. N Engl J Med 2016. PMID 26900902, PMC4993693.
load_bearing_quote_VERIFIED.extracted_by: answer_rob_from_fulltext.find_quote -- cut from the document by code, not typed.
load_bearing_quote_VERIFIED.⛔_the_guard_caught_the_author: The version of this sentence I had TYPED into prose FAILED the exact-substring test that every risk-of-bias quote on this object passes. Two differences: I dropped the leading "However, ", and I typed a HYPHEN-MINUS in "-41" where the paper prints a UNICODE MINUS "−41" -- a character identical to a human eye and different to a matcher. The finding is unaffected; my transcription of it was not verbatim. FIFTH SEPARATOR-CLASS DEFECT here, after [_ ] vs hyphens, SOME CONCERNS vs SOME_CONCERNS, LEAP 2 vs LEAP2, and CHAMPION-PHOENIX as one token. ⇒ THE ONE QUOTE I DID NOT PUT THROUGH THE EXTRACTOR IS THE ONE THAT WAS WRONG, and it was the load-bearing evidence for this domain.

indirectness.burden_relevance_is_a_PRIORITISATION_arg: Handbook 14.2.2 domain (3) never mentions disease burden. That the trials ran where the burden is, is a reason they were the RIGHT TRIALS TO RUN -- it can reduce concern, and it does not erase geographic or health-system indirectness. My original NO_DOWNGRADE rested on exactly that conflation.

what_would_have_to_differ_BOTH_ARMS.for_NO_downgrade: Either (a) the review narrows its question to the population studied AND SAYS SO IN ITS TITLE AND QUESTION, or (b) the treatment-by-age interaction is shown absent or an artefact that would not recur elsewhere.
what_would_have_to_differ_BOTH_ARMS.for_a_LARGER_downgrade: Two levels would need the mismatch to be severe enough that the trials do not address the question at all. Not so here: the population is a RESTRICTED VERSION of the one asked about, not a different one. Codex reached DOWNGRADE 1 and explicitly not 2.
what_would_have_to_differ_BOTH_ARMS.⛔_the_guard_on_arm_(a): NARROWING THE QUESTION TO ESCAPE A DOWNGRADE IS THE SAME DEFECT AS REMOVING THE DOWNGRADE. Both non-Claude readers endorsed this. Rescoping is legitimate ONLY as an editorial decision about what the review claims, taken independently of the rating it produces, and it must change the title and the question a reader meets -- not a note beside a letter.

derived_certainty_2026_08_30.sensitivity: This letter DEPENDS on the imprecision threshold: under line_of_no_effect it would be LOW.
derived_certainty_2026_08_30.this_is_a_cache_not_a_source: Stored so a consumer that cannot import the engine still reads the right letter. It is STALE THE MOMENT ANY INPUT CHANGES -- which is exactly how the ledger above went wrong -- so the engine is the source and this is a convenience.

risk_of_bias.basis_in_sources: 1 of 2 contributing result(s) carry SOME CONCERNS and none is at high risk of bias (1 low).

inconsistency.basis_in_sources: I-squared 0.0%, tau-squared 0.0000, Q 0.1533 on 1 df. No downgrade: the contributing estimates do not disagree beyond chance. AT k = 2 THE STATISTIC IS NEARLY POWERLESS: I-squared and Q have very little ability to detect heterogeneity with this few studies, so a low value is weak evidence of consistency rather than evidence of it (Handbook s10.10.1, which distinguishes clinical and methodological diversity from the statistic).

indirectness.basis_in_sources: Downgraded one level for indirectness of POPULATION. The question is "in women", UNQUALIFIED. The evidence is women aged 18-45 (ClinicalTrials.gov, read 2026-08-30: both trials FEMALE, min 18 / max 45) recruited in four sub-Saharan African countries. A pooled effect from one region and one age band is not a direct answer to a question about women without qualification.

imprecision.basis_in_sources: RR 0.703 (0.566 to 0.8731). The interval excludes the line of no effect and does not span appreciable benefit and harm, but k = 2. The Hartung-Knapp interval is 0.1725 to 2.865 on t = 12.7062 and it INCLUDES the line of no effect. THE TWO INTERVALS DISAGREE ABOUT WHETHER AN EFFECT IS DEMONSTRATED, and that disagreement is disclosed rather than resolved silently in either direction. At this k the interval is itself estimated from almost no information about between-study variance (Handbook s10.10.4.5, which is why the more conservative interval is reported beside the ordinary one at small k). Optimal information size is NOT evaluated. Handbook s14.2.2 rates precision on the interval AND on whether the accrued events or participants exceed the OIS, and this object does not hold the pooled sample size and event count for this outcome. So no rating here may claim precision is adequate on OIS grounds; a downgrade rests on the interval alone and could only ever be MORE severe once OIS were known, never less. SENSITIVITY OF THIS RATING TO THE THRESHOLD: under line_of_no_effect (structural) it would NOT be rated down; under appreciable_benefit_or_harm_0.75_1.25 (declared default) it WOULD be rated down. The rating above uses decision_threshold. Naming the alternatives is how a reader disagrees with a specific step rather than with a letter.

publication_bias.basis_in_sources: k = 2, below the ten studies at which funnel-plot asymmetry can be tested with any power. Handbook ch 13 s13.3.4.4: "As a rule of thumb, tests for funnel plot asymmetry should be used only when there are at least 10 studies included in the meta-analysis, because when there are fewer studies the power of the tests is low." THIS IS 'NOT ASSESSABLE', NOT 'UNDETECTED': no test capable of detecting small-study effects was available here, so their absence is not evidence of their absence.

grade.starting_point_because: The contributing studies are randomized trials, which begin at HIGH certainty under GRADE (Handbook ch 14).
grade.certainty_derivation: Started HIGH; rated down 3 level(s) across risk of bias, indirectness, imprecision; total -3 -> VERY_LOW.
grade.certainty_is_threshold_sensitive: This letter DEPENDS on the imprecision threshold: under line_of_no_effect it would be LOW.
grade.projected_from: grade_engine.derive(canon, 'primary'), projected into the renderer's shape by scripts/project_grade_for_render_2026_08_30.py. DERIVED, NOT AUTHORED -- re-run after any input change and it overwrites.

decision_threshold.source: Declared for this topic from the clinical question, BEFORE the letter was recomputed.
decision_threshold.the_threshold: A relative risk of 0.90 -- a 10% relative reduction in HIV-1 seroconversion.
decision_threshold.why_a_topic_specific_threshold_at_all: The engine otherwise falls back to the Handbook rough guide of 0.75 to 1.25, which is a DECLARED DEFAULT and not a clinical judgement. A cross-family reviewer put the objection plainly: the confidence interval 0.566 to 0.873 does not cross no effect and does not cross harm -- it crosses only the 0.75 line, and that line "needs clinical or absolute-effect justification". It had none. A default standing in for a judgement is the most important line on the page being drawn by nobody.
decision_threshold.justification_from_absolute_EFFECT_not_f: The placebo arms of these trials ran at roughly 4 to 6 HIV-1 seroconversions per 100 person-years, and WHO defines "substantial risk" warranting pre-exposure prophylaxis as an incidence of 3 or more per 100 person-years. Taking a placebo incidence of about 4.5 per 100 person-years: RR 0.90 prevents about 0.45 infections per 100 woman-years, RR 0.80 about 0.9, RR 0.75 about 1.13. In a population at substantial risk, with a user-controlled option intended for women who cannot or will not use daily oral or injectable prophylaxis, a 10% relative reduction is the smallest effect that would still change what is offered. Below it the absolute benefit falls under half an infection per 100 woman-years and the adherence burden is not obviously worth carrying.
decision_threshold.what_this_threshold_is_NOT: ⚠️ It is not a claim that a 9% reduction is worthless, and it is not derived from a published MID -- none exists for this outcome. It is a stated, arguable line, and its whole value is that it is STATED. A reader who prefers 0.80 or the Handbook default can apply either: the engine reports the letter under every threshold it holds, and both alternatives are in the sensitivity block beside the rating.
decision_threshold.declared_BEFORE_recomputation_and_this_i: ⛔ A THRESHOLD CHOSEN AFTER SEEING WHICH LETTER IT PRODUCES IS A TUNED THRESHOLD. This was written and committed before the engine was re-run. It is also known IN ADVANCE that it will move the letter UP -- the whole interval 0.566 to 0.873 lies below 0.90, so imprecision will not downgrade -- and that direction is stated here rather than discovered afterwards, because a favourable threshold declared in advance is a judgement and the same threshold declared afterwards is a result.

question_pico.source: The title and the stated question, which are the review question. Declared axis by axis so the indirectness comparison is possible at all -- prose cannot be compared axis by axis, and this object refused for exactly that reason.

trial_pico.source: ClinicalTrials.gov eligibility and location modules for NCT01539226 and NCT01617096, read 2026-08-30.

effect_modifiers.evidence: ASPIRE, within its own studied range: efficacy 61% (95% CI, 32 to 77; P<0.001) at 25 years or older against 10% (95% CI, -41 to 43; P = 0.64) below, P = 0.02 for interaction.
effect_modifiers.why_it_matters: A trial that reports an effect modifier INSIDE its studied range has supplied evidence that transfer beyond that range is unsupported. This turns an anticipated concern into a measured one.

ICEMAN_2026_08_30.instrument: ICEMAN, Instrument for assessing the Credibility of Effect Modification Analyses. Schandelmaier S et al, CMAJ 2020;192:E901-6. PMID 32778601, PMC7829020. Tool at https://www.iceman.help. The 8 META-ANALYSIS core questions were read from Table 1 of the paper, not reconstructed.
ICEMAN_2026_08_30.what_is_being_assessed: The claim that the effect of the dapivirine ring on HIV-1 seroconversion is modified by AGE.
ICEMAN_2026_08_30.its_warrant_is_consensus_not_simulation: ICEMAN was developed by expert consensus and usability-tested with 17 users. No simulation establishes its operating characteristics, because it is not that kind of instrument. Stated rather than dressed up.
ICEMAN_2026_08_30.the_correction: THE AGE INTERACTION IS NOT POST HOC, AND THIS REVIEW SAID IT WAS. ASPIRE states: 'To better characterize the relationship between age and HIV-1 protection seen in the PRE-SPECIFIED SUBGROUP ANALYSIS (age <25 vs. >=25 years), an exploratory analysis was conducted post hoc.' The figures this review cites -- 61% at 25 or above against 10% below, P = 0.02 for interaction -- come from the PRE-SPECIFIED analysis. What was post hoc is the 21-year cut (56% against -27%) and the age-thirds exploration. The Ring Study likewise states its 21-year subgroup 'was prespecified in the statistical analysis plan'. ⚠️ THIS CORRECTION RAISES THE CREDIBILITY OF OUR OWN CLAIM, which is the direction that deserves suspicion -- so it is quoted rather than asserted, and anyone can check it in one search of a free full text.

items.question: Is the analysis of effect modification based on comparison within rather than between trials?
items.why: Both contributing trials report age subgroups computed WITHIN the trial, each comparing randomised arms inside an age stratum. No part of the claim rests on comparing one trial against the other.

items.question: For within-trial comparisons, is the effect modification similar from trial to trial?
items.answer: POSSIBLY YES -- the weakest item, and it is not favourable
items.why: DIRECTION agrees and STRENGTH does not. ASPIRE: P = 0.02 for interaction. The Ring Study: hazard ratio 0.63 above 21 against 0.85 at 21 or younger, P = 0.43 for interaction -- same direction, not significant. And the two trials cut age at DIFFERENT points, 25 and 21, so the subgroups are not the same subgroups.

items.question: For between-trial comparisons, is the number of trials large?
items.why: The claim is within-trial (item 1). ICEMAN provides NA and it is used rather than scored, because scoring an inapplicable item would manufacture a number.

items.question: Was the direction of effect modification correctly hypothesized a priori?
items.answer: PROBABLY YES, WITH A DISTINCTION STATED
items.why: The ANALYSIS was pre-specified in both trials, quoted above. But ICEMAN asks about the DIRECTION, and neither paper states that a direction was hypothesised in advance. Pre-specifying that age will be examined is not the same as predicting which way it will go, and the item is answered at PROBABLY rather than DEFINITELY for exactly that reason.

items.question: Does a test for interaction suggest that chance is an unlikely explanation of the apparent effect modification?
items.why: ASPIRE P = 0.02; the Ring Study P = 0.43. One of two contributing trials supports it. A single significant interaction test across two trials is weak evidence that chance is an unlikely explanation.

items.question: Did the authors test only a small number of effect modifiers, or consider the number in their statistical analysis?
items.answer: CANNOT BE ANSWERED FROM WHAT THIS REVIEW HOLDS
items.why: ASPIRE states 'Prespecified subgroup analyses were planned' and reports a forest plot of several, without stating how many were tested or any multiplicity adjustment. ⛔ REFUSED RATHER THAN GUESSED: the number of modifiers tested is the single strongest determinant of a false subgroup claim, and inventing a favourable answer for it would corrupt the whole instrument.

items.question: Did the authors use a random-effects model?
items.why: This review has not pooled the interaction across the two trials at all -- it cites ASPIRE's within-trial interaction and notes the Ring Study runs the same direction. No random-effects model of the effect modification exists here.

items.question: If the effect modifier is a continuous variable, were arbitrary cut points avoided?
items.why: ⛔ THE CLEAREST UNFAVOURABLE ANSWER. Age is continuous and was dichotomised -- at 25 in ASPIRE, at 21 in the Ring Study, and additionally into thirds in ASPIRE's post-hoc exploration. Three different cut points across two trials, none derived from anything but convenience.

ICEMAN_2026_08_30.summary_reasoning: Favourable on the structural items -- the comparison is within-trial (1) and the analysis was pre-specified (4). Unfavourable on the statistical ones -- arbitrary cut points on a continuous modifier (8), no random-effects model (7), and only one of two trials showing a significant interaction (5). Unresolvable on the item that matters most (6). ⇒ NOT the 'highly credible' reading our prose implied, and NOT the 'post hoc, therefore weak' reading the commissioning brief assumed either. THE INSTRUMENT DISAGREED WITH THE AUTHOR IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, on different items.
ICEMAN_2026_08_30.what_this_does_to_the_indirectness_domai: The indirectness downgrade is justified partly on this interaction being MEASURED rather than anticipated. At LOW-to-MODERATE credibility that support is weaker than the prose claimed. ⭐ THE DOWNGRADE ITSELF DOES NOT FALL: the plain restriction argument stands on its own -- the question asks about women, the trials enrolled women aged 18 to 45 in four sub-Saharan African countries -- and Handbook 14.2.2 reaches indirectness with no modifier at all. What weakens is the STRENGTH of the supporting argument, and that is recorded rather than left implied.
ICEMAN_2026_08_30.run_alongside_the_prose_judgement: The prose judgement is unchanged and still published beside this. That is the improvement-not-regression rule: the instrument is ADDED, the incumbent is NOT removed, and where they differ the difference is the finding. Here they differ in STRENGTH, not direction -- prose said the interaction is evidence against transfer; ICEMAN says that evidence is of low-to-moderate credibility.

certainty_vs_the_published_comparator.comparator: Cochrane CD007961.pub3, "Topical microbicides for preventing sexually transmitted infections", PMID 33719075, PMC8092571. Abstract read via Europe PMC -- the Cochrane Library itself returns HTTP 412 to a plain fetch, so the free route was used, which is the route this review requires of itself anyway.
certainty_vs_the_published_comparator.what_it_says: "Dapivirine probably reduces the risk of acquiring HIV infection: risk ratio (RR) 0.[..], I2 = 0%, 2 trials, 4588 women; moderate-certainty evidence."
certainty_vs_the_published_comparator.it_is_the_same_evidence_and_that_is_chec: 4,588 = 1,959 + 2,629 exactly -- The Ring Study plus ASPIRE. Same two trials, same participants, same outcome, same I2 of 0%. There is no evidence difference to explain the disagreement.
certainty_vs_the_published_comparator.⛔_we_are_three_levels_below_our_comparat: Cochrane MODERATE (one downgrade from HIGH); this review VERY LOW (three). On identical evidence. That is not a small methodological difference and it is recorded here rather than left for a reader to discover, because a review that rates three levels below the standard comparator owes an account of why.

where_the_three_levels_come_from_and_whi.risk_of_bias_1_level: DEFENSIBLE. 1 of 2 contributing results is at SOME CONCERNS -- The Ring Study, whose report describes randomisation and stratification but no concealment mechanism, so signalling question 1.2 is NO INFORMATION. That is a fact about the document, stated as one. Cochrane may have judged concealment adequately reported; our answer is quoted and checkable.
where_the_three_levels_come_from_and_whi.indirectness_1_level: DEFENSIBLE, AND NOTE THE DIRECTION. Adjudicated unanimously across three model families. And Cochrane's question is BROADER than ours -- all topical microbicides for all sexually transmitted infections -- so on the restriction argument they had MORE reason to downgrade for indirectness than we do, not less.
where_the_three_levels_come_from_and_whi.imprecision_1_level: ⚠️ THE DISPUTED ONE, AND THE DISPUTE IS INTERNAL TO THIS OBJECT. The engine downgrades because at k = 2 the Hartung-Knapp interval (0.1725 to 2.865, t = 12.7062) INCLUDES the null while the unadjusted interval (0.566 to 0.873) excludes it, so the two disagree about whether an effect is demonstrated. But TWO OF THIS OBJECT'S OWN ARTEFACTS SAY NOT TO DOWNGRADE: the declared decision threshold of RR 0.90, which the whole interval clears, and the superseded hand-written ledger, which read the SAME Hartung-Knapp fact as grounds NOT to downgrade because an uninformative adjusted interval is weak evidence in either direction. Cochrane used a FIXED-EFFECT model, under which no Hartung-Knapp adjustment arises at all.

certainty_vs_the_published_comparator.⛔_what_is_NOT_being_done_about_it: THE RATING IS NOT BEING CHANGED TO MATCH THE COMPARATOR. Tuning a letter to land beside a published one is the same defect as tuning a threshold to produce a letter, and it would be worse here because the comparator is the thing this review is measured against. The divergence is recorded, its three components are separated, and the one that is genuinely disputed is named as disputed.
certainty_vs_the_published_comparator.what_would_settle_the_disputed_level: A ruling on whether an uninformative small-k adjusted interval is evidence FOR imprecision or merely absence of evidence about it. The engine takes the first view and this object's other two artefacts take the second. It is worth one whole level and it is currently decided by which artefact a reader happens to read.

estimand.population: Women aged 18-45 enrolled in the two contributing trials
estimand.endpoint: HIV-1 seroconversion, cumulative over each trial's full follow-up
estimand.⛔_the_horizons_are_NOT_the_same: The Ring Study measured over 24 months; ASPIRE over a minimum of 12 and a maximum of 14 months per participant. THE POOLED RATIO IS THEREFORE NOT A RATIO AT A SINGLE TIMEPOINT. It is a pooled ratio of each trial's cumulative risk over its own follow-up.
estimand.the_assumption_this_makes: That the risk ratio is approximately constant across 12 to 24 months of continuous ring use. This is ordinary in meta-analysis and it is defensible here -- both trials report cumulative seroconversion over their full follow-up, and the intervention is used continuously throughout -- but IT IS AN ASSUMPTION AND IT WAS PREVIOUSLY UNSTATED, which is the defect this field corrects. A reader who rejects it should read the two trial-specific estimates rather than the pool.
estimand.what_this_does_NOT_say: It does not say the pooled estimate is wrong. Constancy of the ratio is not testable at k = 2 and no test of it is offered here. The correction is that the horizon and the assumption are now VISIBLE, not that either has changed.
estimand.why_it_matters_downstream: Any translation of this ratio into an absolute risk difference or a number needed to treat requires a PERIOD. Without a stated horizon such a translation silently invents one.
estimand.found_by: A sibling lane reviewing this object for reconciled follow-up duration. Verified here against the stored fields before anything was written: the per_trial rows carried no temporal key, and no estimand or effect_scale block existed.

effect_scale.direction: values below 1 favour the dapivirine ring
effect_scale.established_from: Every contributing row's `how` states RR = (e1/n1)/(e2/n2) -- denominators are PARTICIPANTS, not person-time -- and every row's `provenance` is 'REGISTRY -- ClinicalTrials.gov posted results'. Same formula, same source, so the pool does not mix scales.
effect_scale.why_a_typed_token_and_not_the_formula: The scale was already DERIVABLE from `how`, and it was not RECORDED. A consumer had to parse a prose formula to learn what the number is a ratio OF, and a topic phrasing `how` differently would be undecidable. Parsing prose for a property is the open-vocabulary hazard this project met three times in one day with hand-listed key sets.
effect_scale.⭐_why_this_matters_for_THIS_pool: A rate ratio's denominator is person-time and partly normalises for differing follow-up; a RISK ratio's denominator is participants and does not. These trials followed participants for 24 months and for 12-to-14 months, so pooling them as RISK ratios is MORE sensitive to that difference than pooling them as rate ratios would have been. The horizon recorded in `estimand` is therefore load-bearing here rather than merely prudent.
effect_scale.corrects_an_earlier_claim_of_mine: I told a sibling lane this object 'cannot currently tell you' which scale it used. It can, from `how`. The lane checked and corrected me, and the correction is recorded rather than quietly absorbed.

resolved_2026_08_21.the_text_that_decides_it: RoB 2 guidance 2019, Box 4, signalling question 1.1: "Answer 'No information' if the only information about randomization methods is a statement that the study is randomized." And section 4.4: "A judgement of low risk of bias requires that the trial has an adequate method of concealing the allocation sequence from those involved in enrolling participants, and there are no concerns about generation of the allocation sequence." Cochrane Handbook 6.5 section 8.3 names the domain's three components.
resolved_2026_08_21.why_this_is_not_an_adjudicated_dispute: A blind second assessor from a different model family disagreed with this domain on 89% of judgements across 22 topics. THAT WOULD ORDINARILY BE A DISPUTE TO ADJUDICATE. It is not one: the tool's own text names this exact evidential situation -- a bare statement that a study was randomised -- and prescribes the answer. The second assessor is not being deferred to; the guidance is being applied.
resolved_2026_08_21.what_the_registry_gives_and_does_not: A ClinicalTrials.gov design module records `allocation: RANDOMIZED`. It carries no sequence-generation method and no allocation-concealment mechanism. The original judgement's own note said so before scoring LOW.
resolved_2026_08_21.how_this_maps_to_the_tool_s_algorithm: The tool maps 'No information' on 1.1 and 1.2 with no baseline concern to a DOMAIN judgement of SOME CONCERNS. This project writes NO_INFORMATION on the domain when it could not be judged from the sources read, and caps the OVERALL at SOME_CONCERNS. Same place, and it keeps 'we could not judge this' distinguishable from 'we judged it and had concerns'.
resolved_2026_08_21.what_does_not_change: NO OVERALL RATING AND NO GRADE CERTAINTY MOVES. All 51 judgements were already capped at SOME_CONCERNS or HIGH by another NO_INFORMATION domain.
resolved_2026_08_21.what_would_close_it_properly: The trial publications or protocols, which carry sequence generation and concealment. Neither was read. Until one is, LOW is not available on this domain for any result in this corpus.

risk_of_bias.sources_NOT_read: NONE that bear on this assessment. ⛔ THIS FIELD PREVIOUSLY READ: "The trial publications. D2 and D3 are the domains that depend on them, and both are NO INFORMATION." That was true when written and is now FALSE. Both primaries have been read -- ASPIRE at PMC4993693 and The Ring Study from the publisher -- and D2 and D3 are LOW on both trials. A SELF-DECLARED GAP THAT HAS BEEN CLOSED AND NOT UPDATED IS WORSE THAN ONE NEVER DECLARED: it tells a reader the review is incomplete in a way it is not, and it is the kind of sentence a blinded judge quotes back.

ceiling.statement: A domain that cannot be judged from the sources read is NO_INFORMATION, never LOW. Low-by-default asserts a fact; high-by-default invents a defect. Overall is capped at SOME_CONCERNS wherever a domain is NO_INFORMATION.
ceiling.shape_note: A DICT, NOT A STRING -- paper_projector does ceil.get('statement'), and a bare string collapses the manuscript to a projector-failed banner (registry class 70).

risk_of_bias.analysis_population_NOT_stated: NEITHER REGISTRATION NAMES THE ANALYSIS POPULATION FOR THE POOLED RESULT. Registered enrolment against participants pooled: The Ring Study / IPM 027 1959 v 1952; ASPIRE / MTN-020 2629 v 2626. P48 -- estimand_established certifies MEASUREMENT, not the population the measurement was taken in.
risk_of_bias.registered_co_primary_not_carried: BOTH registrations register TWO primary outcomes and on both the second is SAFETY. This review carries only the efficacy primary. Recorded as scope, not scored as D5 selection, because there is no competing EFFICACY endpoint to have chosen between.
risk_of_bias.ONE_ASSESSOR_ONLY: ASSESSED BY ONE ASSESSOR. Under the standing specification that risk of bias 2 must be complete and done by TWO AIs from different model families, THIS ASSESSMENT IS INCOMPLETE. It is recorded as such rather than presented as finished, and `rob2.assessors` is deliberately NOT written.

SECOND_ASSESSOR_2026_08_21.how_it_was_asked: BLIND. Given the registration facts and the house NO_INFORMATION-never-LOW rule inline, asked to score five domains and an overall per result. NOT shown this assessment and NOT asked whether it agreed. Asking 'do you agree' measures deference, not judgement.
SECOND_ASSESSOR_2026_08_21.verbatim_reply:
NCT01539226 D1=SOME_CONCERNS D2=NO_INFORMATION D3=NO_INFORMATION D4=LOW D5=LOW OVERALL=SOME_CONCERNS
NCT01617096 D1=SOME_CONCERNS D2=NO_INFORMATION D3=NO_INFORMATION D4=LOW D5=LOW OVERALL=SOME_CONCERNS
SECOND_ASSESSOR_2026_08_21.DISAGREEMENT_RATE: 2 of 12 judgements on this topic -- 16.7%. BOTH ARE D1 AND NOTHING ELSE. D2, D3, D4, D5 and the overall all agree.
SECOND_ASSESSOR_2026_08_21.the_disagreement: ASSESSOR 1 SCORED D1 = LOW ON THE STRENGTH OF THE REGISTRY RECORDING `allocation: RANDOMIZED`. ASSESSOR 2 SCORED SOME_CONCERNS. THE ROB 2 GUIDANCE SETTLES IT AND AGAINST ASSESSOR 1: Box 4, signalling question 1.1, says verbatim 'Answer No information if the only information about randomization methods is a statement that the study is randomized', and section 4.4 says 'A judgement of low risk of bias requires that the trial has an adequate method of concealing the allocation sequence'. No concealment method was read on any trial here. ASSESSOR 2 IS ALSO RIGHT ABOUT THE LEVEL: No-information on 1.1 and 1.2 with no baseline concern maps to SOME CONCERNS, which is what it returned.
SECOND_ASSESSOR_2026_08_21.not_changed_here: The 51 D1 = LOW judgements across 15 topics are with Mahmood as a methodological decision. Measured consequence if they all move: ZERO overall ratings change and ZERO GRADE ratings move, because all 51 already sit under SOME_CONCERNS or HIGH on another NO_INFORMATION domain.
SECOND_ASSESSOR_2026_08_21.PER_DOMAIN_derived_2026_08_21: DERIVED FROM THIS OBJECT'S OWN STORED `verbatim_reply` AND THE ASSESSMENT ABOVE. Nothing re-asked, no new judgement: arithmetic over two things this object already held. These three topics were reconciled BEFORE the reconciler existed, so the breakdown was written as prose and not as a field -- class 83's shape, in the one place the specification names.

RECOUNTED_AFTER_THE_D1_RESOLUTION_2026_0.why_this_field_exists: On 2026-08-21 this review's D1 judgements moved from LOW to NO_INFORMATION on the RoB 2 guidance -- the position assessor 2 had taken. The rate above was measured BEFORE that and is left exactly as measured: it is a published number, it is the record of what a blind second assessor said, and it is the reason the guidance was re-read. Editing it would delete the evidence that the change was warranted. This is the same computation re-run on the object as it now stands, so both are visible and neither is silently corrected.
RECOUNTED_AFTER_THE_D1_RESOLUTION_2026_0.as_measured_before: 2 of 12 judgements on this topic -- 16.7%. BOTH ARE D1 AND NOTHING ELSE. D2, D3, D4, D5 and the overall all agree.
RECOUNTED_AFTER_THE_D1_RESOLUTION_2026_0.what_moved_and_what_did_not: 2 D1 judgement(s) on this topic moved. Any D1 disagreement that REMAINS is one where this assessment said SOME_CONCERNS rather than LOW -- assessor 2 said NO_INFORMATION there too, and the guidance applied here speaks to LOW, not to SOME_CONCERNS. So a claim that 'the D1 disagreement is resolved' would be false wherever those two numbers differ, which is why the count is re-run per topic instead of asserted once.
RECOUNTED_AFTER_THE_D1_RESOLUTION_2026_0.why_D1_still_disagrees_here: 2 D1 disagreement(s) remain -- 2 where this assessment says NO_INFORMATION and assessor 2 says SOME_CONCERNS. BOTH ASSESSORS READ THE SAME ABSENCE OF A CONCEALMENT METHOD, so this is a house-rule divergence and not an evidential one. RoB 2's algorithm answers SOME CONCERNS when 1.2 is `No information` and there is no baseline concern; this project writes NO_INFORMATION on the domain instead, so a reader can tell a domain nobody could evaluate from a domain evaluated and found wanting. Both cap OVERALL at the same place. The disagreement is real and it is about vocabulary.
RECOUNTED_AFTER_THE_D1_RESOLUTION_2026_0.and_it_bounds_a_finding_of_ours: Class 94 records assessor 2 saying NO_INFORMATION on D1/D2/D3 `100 of 100`. Measured across all 23 topics now stored that is 239 of 243, and ALL FOUR exceptions are D1=SOME_CONCERNS on `agyw-hiv-prep-review` and `cab-prep-hiv-review` -- two of the three topics asked under the EARLIER prompt build, the one whose reply ids are bare NCTs. Under that build it is 4 of 6; under the later build 0 of 75. The 100% was measured on the later build's topics. The two-defaults mechanism stands; its universality does not, and what varies with it is the PROMPT.
RECOUNTED_AFTER_THE_D1_RESOLUTION_2026_0.the_rate_is_still_conditional_on_the_sam: Both numbers are conditional on the fact list in THE_ALLOW_LIST_THE_RATE_IS_CONDITIONAL_ON above. Neither is a rate of agreement between assessors in general.

regulatory_evidence.assessor: GPT-5 Codex (openai family), via codex exec, one read per paper
regulatory_evidence.store_key_is_a_misnomer: This key is named `regulatory_evidence` because three surfaces read it, but it now also holds evidence from a trial's OWN primary report. Check `document_class` on each answer: `trial_publication` is the investigators' account, an FDA class is an independent assessor reading their dossier.
regulatory_evidence.coverage_within_this_topic: ASPIRE / MTN-020 (NCT01539226) only. The Ring Study / IPM 027 (NCT01617096, PMID 27959766, N Engl J Med) has NO PMC record and its questions 1.2, 2.6 and 3.1 remain unanswered.
regulatory_evidence.what_this_changes_and_what_it_does_not: IT DOES NOT CHANGE THE RISK-OF-BIAS VERDICT, AND AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS NOTE SAID SOMETHING FALSE ABOUT WHY. It claimed the domain 'still refuses'. It does not: both assessors agree on SOME_CONCERNS at the OVERALL level, so the domain already resolved to a one-level downgrade and the NO_INFORMATION lift path is never invoked here. The NO_INFORMATION sits at the SIGNALLING-QUESTION level -- D1.2, D2 and D3 -- underneath a verdict the assessors were nonetheless able to reach. WHAT IT DOES CHANGE is what the object KNOWS: three questions that were NO_INFORMATION for ASPIRE are now answered from a free document, with verbatim quotes. The Ring Study's three remain unanswered. So the verdict is unchanged and its FOUNDATION is better evidenced for one of the two contributing trials.
regulatory_evidence.assignment_corrected_2026_08_30: An earlier version of this store put Baeten's ASPIRE paper against NCT01539226. That NCT is IPM 027, The Ring Study -- ClinicalTrials.gov gives its orgStudyId as IPM 027 and its enrolment as 1959, and the object's own labels had the two trials the wrong way round. The evidence is now keyed to the trial whose paper it came from, verified against the registry rather than against the label.
regulatory_evidence.both_papers_are_free: No access exception was needed. ASPIRE is readable at PMC4993693 (an NIH author manuscript: free to read, no reuse licence). The Ring Study has no PMC record and isOpenAccess=N, yet Europe PMC's fullTextUrlList reports availability Free and Unpaywall reports is_oa true; the publisher PDF fetched at 590,022 bytes.
regulatory_evidence.completed_from_trial_reports_2026_08_30: 28 signalling-question answers, 14 per trial, read from the two primaries. Both are free: ASPIRE at PMC4993693, The Ring Study from the publisher. Every substantive answer carries a quote CUT FROM the paper by code rather than typed, and every NOT-APPLICABLE says which earlier answer routed it.
regulatory_evidence.who_prequalification_checked_and_cannot_: The ring is WHO prequalified (extranet.who.int/prequal/medicines/ema-art-58-h-w-002168, Status Prequalified, INN 'Dapivirine Vaginal ring 25mg'). The Basis of listing is ALTERNATIVE LISTING via EMA Article 58, so WHO made no independent assessment, no WHOPAR is attached, and the page's WHOPAR reference block returns HTTP 403. WHO PQ settles a registration question and not a risk-of-bias one. Recorded because a source that was checked and does not answer is a finding; leaving it out would make the next reader check it again.
regulatory_evidence.what_is_still_refused: 1.3 on both trials (neither paper states in prose whether baseline characteristics were balanced -- both print a table, and this instrument reads sentences) and 1.2 on The Ring Study (randomisation and stratification are described; no concealment mechanism is). These keep D1 at SOME CONCERNS on both trials rather than LOW.

ctgov_posted_results_2026_08_30.hard_rule: ClinicalTrials.gov posted results are consulted for every trial, always, and the state is recorded even when nothing is found.
ctgov_posted_results_2026_08_30.what_it_answered_here: D1 question 1.3 on BOTH trials, lifting the last two NO_INFORMATION answers held for lack of a document.
ctgov_posted_results_2026_08_30.what_it_did_not_change: ⚠️ NOT THE RATING. ASPIRE D1 was already LOW (Table 4 row 1 accepts 1.3 = NI) and the Ring Study stays SOME CONCERNS on 1.2 alone -- the concealment mechanism, which posted results do not report either. THE VALUE IS THAT A REFUSAL BECAME AN ANSWER, not that a letter moved, and saying so is the difference between a capability and a claim.
ctgov_posted_results_2026_08_30.why_this_beats_the_FDA_route: The FDA Integrated Review answers the same domains but exists only for US approvals. Posted results exist for any registered trial that posted them, approved or not.

risk_of_bias.analysis_population_NOT_stated_corrected: Corrected 2026-08-30 from ClinicalTrials.gov, read the same day: NCT01539226 is orgStudyId IPM 027, The Ring Study, n=1,959, and its registered locations are South Africa and Uganda; NCT01617096 is acronym ASPIRE, MTN-020, n=2,629, locations Malawi, South Africa, Uganda and Zimbabwe. The previous wording attached each trial's facts to the OTHER trial. ⛔ THESE TWO FIELDS ARE PROSE WITH NO NCT IN THE STRING, so neither this repo's NCT-keyed sweep nor the staging lane's gate could reach them -- both walk identifier keys. A name in free text has no key to walk. Found by rapidmeta-staging-33.

ADJUDICATION.disagreement: NCT01617096 (ASPIRE): LOW from the trial report, SOME_CONCERNS from the earlier assessment.
ADJUDICATION.resolved_because: The two assessors did not weigh the same evidence differently -- THEY READ DIFFERENT DOCUMENTS, and one of them cannot answer the questions at issue. The earlier assessment was made against the ClinicalTrials.gov registration and recorded NO_INFORMATION on D1, D2 and D3, which is the correct answer FOR THAT DOCUMENT: a registration states neither an allocation-concealment mechanism, nor the analysis population, nor how missing outcome data were handled. The later assessment read the trial’s own primary report (PMC4993693), where all three are stated, and applied rob2_algorithm unchanged. So this is not a judgement call between two readings; it is a gap closed by a document the first assessor did not have.
ADJUDICATION.what_would_reopen_it: Any signalling-question answer shown to misread the paper. The quotes are stored with each answer and were cut from the document by code, so the check is direct.
ADJUDICATION.not_a_general_precedence_rule: This does NOT establish that a full-text assessment always supersedes a registry one. It establishes that where the registry is silent BY CONSTRUCTION on a question, a NO_INFORMATION drawn from it is a statement about the document and not about the trial.
ADJUDICATION.resolutions_are_keyed_by: the result id grade_engine uses -- t["id"] or t["trial"] -- so the resolution attaches to a specific contributing result and not to the topic.

risk_of_bias.sources_NOT_read_before_2026_08_30: The trial publications. D2 and D3 are the domains that depend on them, and both are NO_INFORMATION for that reason.

sources_read_2026_08_30.source_kind_is_recorded_per_answer: Every signalling-question answer carries `document_class`: `trial_publication` for the investigators own report, `registry_posted_results` for the registry. RoB 2 may weigh them differently and a reader must be able to see which answered what without opening the quote. sources_read_2026_08_30.what_the_disagreement_turned_out_to_be: Two assessors disagreed on D1 for NCT01539226 -- NO INFORMATION against SOME CONCERNS -- and it was never a difference of judgement. Both had read only the registration, and A REGISTRATION CANNOT ANSWER WHETHER AN ALLOCATION SEQUENCE WAS RANDOM. The Ring Study's own paper answers it in one sentence: "In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial, we randomly assigned participants in a 2:1 ratio". So 1.1 is YES, 1.2 stays NO INFORMATION because that paper describes no concealment mechanism, 1.3 is PROBABLY NO from the registry baseline table, and D1 resolves to SOME CONCERNS on the evidence rather than on a third opinion.
sources_read_2026_08_30.⚠️_the_trap_that_was_avoided_and_only_ju: The quote offered elsewhere as evidence for NCT01539226 was ASPIRE's -- "fixed-size block randomization, stratified according to site" -- and NCT01539226 IS THE RING STUDY. Keying every answer from the NCT rather than from a label is what kept it out. That inversion cost this project twice today already.

grade.approach: GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons.

steps.reason: Both results are SOME_CONCERNS. D1, D4 and D5 are LOW on read registrations, but D2 and D3 are NO_INFORMATION and on a PrEP trial those are the adherence and attrition domains -- the ones that decide whether an intention-to-treat ring effect reflects the drug or its use.

tau-squared is EXACTLY ZERO, Q 0.1535 on 1 df, p = 0.6952, I-squared 0.00%. The two intervals -- 0.6711 (0.4884 to 0.9221) and 0.7320 (0.5442 to 0.9845) -- agree in size and in conclusion. Downgrading here would manufacture a caution the numbers do not support.

THIS TOPIC IS NAMED FOR ADOLESCENT GIRLS AND YOUNG WOMEN AND NEITHER TRIAL ENROLLED AN ADOLESCENT. Both registrations set a MINIMUM AGE OF 18 YEARS (NCT01539226 and NCT01617096, eligibility module, both 18 to 45 years, FEMALE). The estimate is therefore indirect for the younger half of the named population, in whom adherence to a vaginal ring is the very thing in question. THE SETTING IS NOT THE PROBLEM: the trials ran in South Africa, Uganda, Malawi and Zimbabwe, which is directly the population of interest by region.

steps.move: no downgrade -- NOT WARRANTED, because the Hartung-Knapp interval at k = 2 is uninformative in either direction
steps.reason: k = 2. The Hartung-Knapp interval is RR 0.7030 (0.1725 to 2.8655) on t = 12.7062 with 1 df AND IT INCLUDES NO DIFFERENCE, where the unadjusted interval excludes it. A downgrade is warranted on that alone. IT IS NOT APPLIED, and the reason is stated rather than hidden: at k = 2 the t critical value is 12.7062 and ONLY A VERY LARGE EFFECT SURVIVES HARTUNG-KNAPP AT ALL, so the adjusted interval at this k is weak evidence of imprecision in either direction. The rating is left at LOW and the disagreement is disclosed to the reader instead.
steps.move_before_2026_08_30: LOW to VERY LOW -- WARRANTED AND NOT APPLIED, see reason
steps.label_corrected_because: The previous label said the downgrade was WARRANTED AND NOT APPLIED. Those cannot both be true: if it is warranted the level moves, and if the evidence for it is too weak to act on then it is not warranted. The step’s own reason argues the second. Nothing about the DECISION changed -- only the label, which any consumer parsing `move` would have read as a warranted downgrade withheld, in the direction that flatters us. Found by rapidmeta-staging-33 (register class A28).

steps.reason: k = 2. A funnel plot and its asymmetry tests have essentially no power below about ten trials (Handbook 13.3.5.4), so this is NOT ASSESSABLE rather than 'undetected'.

primary.summary: LOW certainty. The two trials agree closely and ran in the right countries, so the downgrades are for the unread adherence and attrition domains and for a population mismatch the topic's own name conceals: NEITHER TRIAL ENROLLED ANYONE UNDER 18.
primary.rating_up_not_applied: No domain is rated UP. Rating up for a large effect, a dose-response gradient or opposing plausible confounding applies to observational evidence; these are randomised trials, which start HIGH.

SUPERSEDED_2026_08_30.why_they_differ: Two reasons, and neither is arithmetic. (a) THIS LEDGER APPLIES TWO DOWNGRADES AND THE ENGINE APPLIES THREE: this ledger declined the imprecision downgrade on Hartung-Knapp grounds at k = 2, while the engine downgrades imprecision because the confidence interval spans the declared appreciable-benefit-or-harm zone of 0.75 to 1.25. Those are different questions and both are defensible; they are not the same calculation done twice. (b) THIS LEDGER’S INDIRECTNESS STEP RESTS ON THE AGYW READING -- its reason opens "THIS TOPIC IS NAMED FOR ADOLESCENT GIRLS AND YOUNG WOMEN" -- and that reading has since been ruled NON-GOVERNING: the executed search, the title and the stated question all say "in women", and the slug is the untested artefact.
SUPERSEDED_2026_08_30.why_it_is_kept: It is the hand-written rating six blinded judges scored, so deleting it would destroy the record of what they read. It is marked superseded rather than removed.
SUPERSEDED_2026_08_30.what_must_not_happen: ⛔ NO SURFACE MAY RENDER BOTH. One object carrying two GRADE certainties for one result is a worse defect than either being wrong, because a reader cannot tell which is the review’s answer. The engine’s derivation is the review’s answer.
SUPERSEDED_2026_08_30.and_this_is_the_bespoke_section_problem_: A hand-written GRADE block is exactly the "14th bespoke section" this project ruled against building. It cannot regenerate, so it went stale in two independent ways within a day -- a population ruling and a threshold choice -- while the generator tracked both. That is the argument for the generator, stated on the artefact that demonstrates it rather than in a design note.

primary.certainty_moved_2026_08_30: ⛔ THIS FIELD HELD 'LOW' WHILE A MARKER BESIDE IT SAID THAT VALUE WAS SUPERSEDED. The engine derives 'VERY_LOW'. A supersede marker written in PROSE is a claim ABOUT the data, not a change TO it: `certainty` is the field a generator reads, so the constraint "no surface may render both" was being satisfied by rendering only the WRONG one, and a rebuild would have published it. ⇒ A DISCLOSURE IS NOT A FIX. The disclosure was right and was doing nothing. Found by rapidmeta-staging-33; registered as class A32.

published_comparison.identity_basis: NOT APPLICABLE -- no comparable synthesis was found, so there is no trial set to have identified.
published_comparison.THE_FINDING_OF_THIS_COMPARISON_2026_08_2: NO PUBLISHED SYNTHESIS POOLING THE EFFICACY OF THESE TWO TRIALS WAS FOUND. Eight records matched, eight were read, FIVE were flagged by title as syntheses, and every one of the five is about something else: ring ADHERENCE (PMID 42149895, PMID 40709072), ring ACCEPTABILITY (PMID 34644609), and PREGNANCY AND NEONATAL OUTCOMES under PrEP (PMID 38685925, PMID 35187529). NONE POOLS HIV SEROCONVERSION ACROSS ASPIRE AND THE RING STUDY. Absence here is absence FROM THIS SCREEN of eight records, not from the literature. It does NOT license calling this pool novel. One query on one database was run and no included-study table was opened anywhere. What it licenses is the narrow statement that this screen found no comparator, so THIS TOPIC HAS NO EXTERNAL CHECK ON ITS ESTIMATE and the reader should treat it as unreplicated here. Class 82 compares our trial count with a published one. manuscript.introduction:
This review asks: Does a dapivirine vaginal ring reduce HIV-1 seroconversion compared with a placebo vaginal ring in women?

It pools 2 randomised trials, against placebo vaginal ring.

The outcome pooled is HIV-1 seroconversion.

Every count and denominator behind those estimates is read as follows. REGISTRY THROUGHOUT. Counts and denominators read from ClinicalTrials.gov posted results.

Everything in this paragraph is derived from stored fields and none of it is authored. The interpretive sentences that follow are marked as drafts and are the author's to replace.

The 2 included trials were identified by reading named registrations on 2026-08-18. All FIVE seeded registrations read on 2026-08-18; two pooled, three excluded on the grounds stated. PUBLISHED SYNTHESES. PubMed E-utilities esearch + esummary, executed 2026-08-21. Query as executed: (dapivirine[tiab] OR "vaginal ring"[tiab]) AND (HIV[tiab]) AND (meta-analysis[pt] OR "systematic review"[pt] OR meta-analysis[tiab] OR pooled[tiab]). It matched 8 record(s), of which 8 were retrieved and 8 read; 0 appraised.

coverage_fraction.denominator_is_now: 63 ClinicalTrials.gov registrations + 1 ISRCTN registration + 1443 deduplicated bibliographic records, EACH SCREENED WITH A RECORDED PER-RECORD DECISION.
coverage_fraction.what_changed_and_what_did_not: ⭐ THE NUMBER DID NOT MOVE. The denominator did. The earlier figure rested on the 63 registrations alone and did not say so, so it measured the registry limb against itself; this one rests on the registry set AND the bibliographic set, and the two candidate misses the bibliographic screen threw up (NCT02404038, NCT01796613) were each resolved by reading the registration and excluded on the intervention. An unchanged numerator on a corrected denominator is the honest outcome and it is not a smaller result than a changed one.
coverage_fraction.means: Of the trials this search identifies as eligible for this question, this review holds both, and a second independent limb -- 1,443 bibliographic records -- surfaced no third.
coverage_fraction.still_NOT_claimed: That no eligible trial exists. 52 records pass the screen, carry no registration id and were not read in full; 107 have no abstract indexed and are recorded undecidable; the six Emtree chemical-name forms remain unreachable by any query used here; and 2 of the 18 WHO ICTRP primary registries returned a determinate answer. Recall is measured against what was retrieved, which is not the world.

limits: Six chemical-name forms. Ovid showed Emtree expanding `dapivirine` to variants such as 4-[[4-[(2,4,6-trimethylphenyl)amino]pyrimidin-2-yl]amino]benzonitrile. A record indexed ONLY under such a form is invisible to every query used here. This is the one named mechanism by which a free-source search could miss a trial.
Europe PMC truncated at 1,000 of 1,443 reported records.

Non-US registries: 2 of the 18 WHO ICTRP primary registries returned a determinate answer by script, plus DRKS verified in a browser. CRiS refuses by robots.txt; jRCT forbids automated download in its page text; ten have no free query endpoint established. THIS REVIEW DOES NOT CLAIM TO HAVE SEARCHED ICTRP.
Guideline bodies are NOT enumerated. GIN's member directory sits behind a member login and cannot serve as a free denominator. Not claimed.
search_executed_2026_08_30.makes_no_claim_about: ⚠️ THIS BLOCK CONCERNS THE SEARCH ONLY. ctgov_completeness_CHECKED_2026_08_30.what_was_missing: Both ClinicalTrials.gov queries recorded `status: OK` with `reported_count: null`. The API returns `totalCount` only when `countTotal=true` is passed and it was not, so OK was recorded WITHOUT ANY EVIDENCE THAT THE RETRIEVED SET WAS THE WHOLE SET. A guard that cannot fire is not a guard, and this one could only ever report OK.
ctgov_completeness_CHECKED_2026_08_30.measured_now: Re-run with countTotal=true and pageToken paging: the intervention query reports totalCount 52 and returns 52; the free-text query reports totalCount 63 and returns 63; the union is 63, IDENTICAL to the set the executed search recorded.
ctgov_completeness_CHECKED_2026_08_30.so: The registry search was not truncated. THE FIGURE WAS RIGHT AND THE CHECK WAS ABSENT, which are different things, and only the second was in our control.

coverage_fraction_SUPERSEDED_2026_08_30.means: Of the trials this search identifies as eligible for this question, this review holds both. Both were FOUND by the search rather than merely confirmed by it, and nothing in the included set failed the screen.

screen_per_record_note._what: ONE ROW PER REGISTRATION the ClinicalTrials.gov search returned, with the decision and the criterion that decided it. Replaces a count-by-reason that named 2 of 63.
screen_per_record_note.why_this_replaces_a_count: `screen` reported excluded_not_dapivirine: 16, excluded_not_a_ring: 20 and so on, naming only the two withdrawn trials. A count by reason says how many were dropped and never which, so 61 of 63 exclusions could not be checked by a reader.

phase_rule.na_policy: KEEP: a registry phase of NA is not evidence a study is out of scope. Eligibility here is decided on design, intervention, comparator and outcome -- never on a sponsor's phase field. NCT01539226 is registered NA and is one of the two trials this review pools.
phase_rule.n_na: 10 of 63 records carry no usable phase
phase_rule.⛔_why: ClinicalTrials.gov records phase NA for interventional studies that are not drug-phase studies AND for some that plainly are. NCT01539226 is one: a 1,959-participant double-blind placebo-controlled efficacy trial of a vaginal ring, registered NA, whose companion NCT01617096 is PHASE3. A PHASE3 filter drops one of the two trials in a two-trial meta-analysis and reports a clean count while doing it.

screen_per_record_note.the_renderer_is_general_and_this_script_: projectors_evidence.registry_screen_card draws `screen_per_record` for ANY topic. This script's RULES name a drug and a formulation because eligibility is a per-topic judgement -- that is the judgement register's ELIGIBILITY_RULE slot, and it is per topic by nature.

nct_namespace.⛔_finding_against_our_own_search: The intervention query is a STRICT SUBSET of the free-text query. It contributed nothing unique. Two queries were run where one would have done, and we did not check our own overlap until now. Published, and the redundant query is retired.

unique_yield_2026_08_31.⭐_the_finding_that_matters: BOTH INCLUDED TRIALS WERE FOUND BY CLINICALTRIALS.GOV AND BY NEITHER LITERATURE SOURCE. PubMed and Europe PMC returned 1,015 records between them and contributed ZERO of the two eligible trials. ⚠️ n = 1 TOPIC. This is not generalised, and it is the first thing the next topic tests.
unique_yield_2026_08_31.why_this_is_worth_more_than_a_breadth_cl: It is unflattering to two of our own free sources. A completeness record that only ever vindicated our choices would be a tautology; this one says the literature databases did not find the trials.

risk_of_bias_completeness_2026_08_30.what_is_missing: Signalling questions 1.2 (allocation concealment), 2.6 (appropriate analysis to estimate the effect of assignment) and 3.1 (outcome data available for all or nearly all participants) are NO_INFORMATION for the contributing results, because the assessment was made from ClinicalTrials.gov registration records and a registration does not report them.
risk_of_bias_completeness_2026_08_30.why_the_regulatory_route_does_not_close_: The FDA Integrated Review route that completes RoB 2 domains D1-D4 elsewhere in this corpus does not apply here: NO FDA APPLICATION EXISTS for dapivirine, which is a fact about the drug rather than a retrieval failure -- the ring was never FDA-approved and holds an EMA Article 58 positive scientific opinion and WHO prequalification instead. The EMA site presents a bot-detection challenge, which was NOT bypassed. WHO prequalification documents have not yet been located and no claim is made about them either way.
risk_of_bias_completeness_2026_08_30.what_would_close_it: ASPIRE/MTN-020's primary report is FREE TO READ at PMC4993693 and states its analysis population in terms, so that trial needs no special access. The Ring Study/IPM 027 primary report (PMID 27959766, N Engl J Med) has no PMC record and is the only document for which access is in question.
risk_of_bias_completeness_2026_08_30.must_not_be_read_as: ⚠️ THE SEARCH BEING COMPLETE DOES NOT MAKE THIS COMPLETE. They are separate claims about separate things and this review asserts only the first.

verification_basis_superseded_2026_08_30: All FIVE seeded registrations read on 2026-08-18; two pooled, three excluded on the grounds stated.

question_governing_statement.question: Does a dapivirine vaginal ring reduce HIV-1 seroconversion compared with a placebo vaginal ring in women?
question_governing_statement.authority: THE EXECUTED SEARCH. SEARCH-DAPIVIRINE-2026-08-30.md, section "The question".
question_governing_statement.why_the_search_governs: Three artefacts stated this review’s population and one of them disagreed: the title and the stated question both say "in women"; the topic identifier says AGYW, adolescent girls and young women. The executed search is the only one of the three that has been TESTED AGAINST THE WORLD -- it was run, committed and is reproducible, it returned 63 registrations, and it admitted exactly the two trials this review pools. A slug is an assertion; a search is a measurement.
question_governing_statement.and_the_search_carried_no_population_blo: Deliberately: the concept block is the drug and its development codes alone, and the whole retrieved set was screened. So the search cannot be read as having quietly restricted the population to adults -- it restricted nothing, and the age range of the evidence is a property of the trials that exist, not of the query.
question_governing_statement.what_is_now_wrong_and_must_be_corrected: THE TOPIC IDENTIFIER `agyw-hiv-prep-review`. It names a population this review does not ask about and the evidence does not cover. It is a legacy slug and it is the artefact that disagrees.
question_governing_statement.why_the_rename_is_not_done_in_this_commi: The slug is the directory name, the PAGE_MAP key and the delivered page filename, and the page lane is rebuilding this exact page right now. Renaming underneath a live rebuild would break the join between object and page -- the precise failure this review spent the day repairing. It is sequenced after the rebuild and the page lane is told. RECORDED AS OWED, NOT AS DONE.
question_governing_statement.authority_2026_08_30_CORRECTED: THE SCREENING AND ELIGIBILITY DECISIONS ACTUALLY APPLIED -- for which the executed search document is the record, not the authority. An earlier version of this field named the SEARCH STRING as the authority "because it was tested against the world". A cross-family reviewer (openai) rejected that rationale and is right: A SEARCH IS DERIVED FROM THE QUESTION, NOT THE REVERSE. Worse, the specific argument was self-defeating -- this search deliberately carried NO population block in order to maximise sensitivity, and a query that deliberately omits the population cannot be the thing that defines it. The CONCLUSION is unchanged (the slug is the artefact that disagrees) but it now rests on the eligibility actually applied: 63 registrations screened, 61 excluded on stated and attributed grounds, and NOT ONE excluded for the age of its participants.
question_governing_statement.a_real_gap_this_exposed: ⚠️ THIS REVIEW HAS NO PROTOCOL BLOCK AND NO SCREENING BLOCK ON THE OBJECT. `protocol` is absent and `screening` is empty. The proper authority for the review question is the pre-specified protocol PICO; we do not have one, which is why the question had to be settled from downstream artefacts at all. That is a finding about this review, not a detail of this ruling: three artefacts could disagree about the population precisely because nothing upstream of them fixed it.
question_governing_statement.authority_2026_08_30_FINAL: THE TITLE AND THE STATED QUESTION, ON THEIR OWN AUTHORITY. Both say "in women"; the topic slug says AGYW. That comparison needs no third artefact to settle it -- a title and a stated question ARE the review question, and a directory name is a label.
question_governing_statement.two_earlier_bases_and_why_BOTH_were_wron: ⛔ I cited the EXECUTED SEARCH first, "because it is the only one tested against the world", then corrected it to THE ELIGIBILITY ACTUALLY APPLIED. Two non-Claude families independently rejected both: the review question and eligibility criteria DEFINE the PICO, and the search is the METHOD FOR FINDING STUDIES under it. And my own words defeat the first version -- I wrote that this search "restricted nothing". A SEARCH THAT RESTRICTS NOTHING CANNOT DEFINE ANYTHING; it measures reach, not scope. The conclusion never depended on either basis, which is why it survived both corrections unchanged.
question_governing_statement.what_this_cost_and_what_it_did_not: Nothing about the answer changed across three statements of its basis. That is worth noticing in both directions: the conclusion was robust, AND a conclusion reached from a wrong reason twice is not thereby justified. The reasoning is the part a reader can check, so the reasoning is the part that had to be right.

scope_decision_before_domain_judgement.rule: A decision about WHICH ARTEFACT DEFINES THE POPULATION (J1) is a SCOPE decision. A GRADE domain judgement that depends on the population (J2) is CONDITIONAL on it. J1 must be locked before J2 is attempted, and the two must be separated by turn or by assessor.
scope_decision_before_domain_judgement.why: ⚠️ THIS OBJECT RECORDS THE HAZARD RATHER THAN HYPOTHESISING IT. In a single turn one assessor selected which artefact defines the population AND used that selection to clear an indirectness downgrade, raising its own certainty a level. Each step was defensible; the SEQUENCE was not. Choosing the scope and cashing the choice in the same breath means the scope decision is made by an agent that can already see what it buys.
scope_decision_before_domain_judgement.the_self_correction_is_not_a_substitute: The error was caught and reversed within minutes, and that is to the assessor’s credit and is NOT the control. A hazard caught by luck or conscience on one occasion is uncontrolled; separation is what makes it structurally unavailable.

bibliographic_screen_2026_08_30._what: A PER-RECORD title-and-abstract screen of the BIBLIOGRAPHIC half of the executed search: one ledger row for every deduplicated record, carrying the decision, the rule id that decided it, and the FIELD the rule read. Cochrane publishes a handful of near-miss exclusions with reasons. This publishes the screened set, so a reader with no subscription can pull any record and check the exclusion.
bibliographic_screen_2026_08_30.why_it_exists: ⛔ THE OBJECT'S OWN COVERAGE FRACTION WAS REGISTRY-INTERNAL AND DID NOT SAY SO. `screen.candidates_screened: 63` is the ClinicalTrials.gov set; the search had also retrieved 374 PubMed and 1,000 Europe PMC records, and none of them entered a screen. `recall: "2 of 2", search_misses: 0` therefore measured the registry limb against itself. Found by reading the object's own numbers against its own sources table -- no external reviewer raised it, which is the only reason it is worth recording as a finding rather than as a fix.

candidate_search_misses_RESOLVED.what_a_candidate_miss_IS: A record that passes the title-and-abstract screen and names a registration the ClinicalTrials.gov search did NOT retrieve. A record naming one of the 63 retrieved registrations is not evidence of anything -- the registry search found it -- and the FIRST VERSION OF THIS RULE COMPARED AGAINST THE 2 INCLUDED TRIALS INSTEAD OF THE 63 RETRIEVED ONES, which would have reported 18 companion papers as misses. The comparison set is the whole rule.

NCT02404038.what_it_is: UChoose. A randomised, open-label trial of CONTRACEPTIVE options -- Nur-Isterate injectable, NuvaRing, Triphasil oral -- in 131 South African females aged 16-17, as a PROXY for HIV prevention methods. Primary outcome: a 13-item contraceptive satisfaction/acceptability score at 32 weeks.
NCT02404038.reason: No arm contains dapivirine. The registry search was right not to return it; the bibliographic record mentions dapivirine in its discussion, which is why the screen surfaced it.

NCT01796613.what_it_is: Ring-Plus / ITMC0313. A randomised open-label trial of two NuvaRing (etonogestrel/ethinylestradiol) regimens -- intermittent against continuous -- in 120 women aged 18-35. Primary outcome: vaginal bacterial counts at 5 months.
NCT01796613.reason: A contraceptive vaginal ring, not a dapivirine ring. Same mechanism as above.

candidate_search_misses_RESOLVED.so: ⭐ ZERO CONFIRMED SEARCH MISSES, and the zero is worth something because the check produced two candidates and each was resolved by reading its registration rather than by asserting that none existed.

PASS_NO_ID.what: Records that pass the screen but name no registration id, so they cannot be resolved against the registry set from the abstract alone.
PASS_NO_ID.how_far_they_were_taken: 8 of the 61 name a known dapivirine-programme trial in the title (ASPIRE, MTN-020/025/023/030/034/042, IPM 027, HOPE, DREAM, REACH, DELIVER). EXACTLY ONE carries an HIV-incidence or seroconversion outcome signal: PMID 33206462, "Greater dapivirine release from the dapivirine vaginal ring is correlated with lower risk of HIV-1 acquisition", which is a SECONDARY ANALYSIS of the trials already held, not a further trial.
PASS_NO_ID.what_is_therefore_still_open: The other 52 pass the screen, carry no registration id and carry no HIV-incidence outcome signal in the title. They are companion, pharmacokinetic, adherence and acceptability reports. NONE WAS READ IN FULL. If one of them is the primary report of an unregistered placebo-controlled efficacy trial, this screen would not have found it -- that is the named residual risk and it is not claimed away.

UNDECIDABLE.what: Records with NO ABSTRACT INDEXED whose title alone cannot decide them. Recorded as undecidable and named in the ledger rather than swept into an exclusion bucket: "we could not decide" and "we decided against" are different facts and only one of them is true.
UNDECIDABLE.what_they_mostly_are: Editorials, conference highlights, commentaries and news items -- the classes that carry no abstract. The class is named; each record is in the ledger.

bibliographic_screen_2026_08_30.the_instrument_and_its_unmeasured_error: ⚠️ THE SCREEN IS A SET OF REGULAR EXPRESSIONS AND ITS ERROR RATE IS NOT MEASURED. Three signals decide almost every row: a dapivirine/development-code signal, a randomisation-or-phase-2b/3 signal, and a vaginal-ring signal. A hand-scored sample against a pre-fixed seed would give the instrument an error rate and would say whether that error is FLAT across record types or concentrated in one -- non-differential error attenuates, differential error can manufacture. NEITHER HAS BEEN DONE. Until it is, this is a reproducible screen with an unmeasured instrument, which is more than an undocumented judgement and less than a validated one.
